_readme: Shared golden test vectors for compute_breakdown/verdict_for - THIS FILE is the source of truth, not any one implementation (ADR-0001 as amended by ADR-0007). Python (src/hdttools/api/breakdown.py), Kotlin (android/.../domain/Breakdown.kt) and the coming TypeScript port are all implementations tested against it; when one disagrees, resolve it here and record the decision in a case _note. Rounding rule: ties round half-UP (toward +infinity, like Kotlin roundToInt and JS Math.round), never Python round-half-to-even - see the rounding_half_way_* cases. See TESTING.md's cross-platform section and tests/test_breakdown_golden_vectors.py. Field names are snake_case, matching the /api/breakdown wire convention - the Kotlin loader maps to its own camelCase data classes. actual_lb/limit_lb are rounded whole numbers (Python parses its actualLabel/limitLabel strings back to int; Kotlin rounds its raw Double) - this tests the math, not display formatting, which each platform already tests separately. 'requires' lists capability tags a case depends on; every runner keeps its own set of supported tags and FAILS a case that names a tag outside it (never skips), so a new capability can't be silently ignored by a port. Besides the row figures, each case asserts expected.headline/subline (the verdict text) and, per row, 'badge' (e.g. '380 lb to spare', '250 lb over', 'Not enough info') and 'note'. Android words two rows' notes differently on purpose (Tow Vehicle Total and Combined Rig Weight spell out their arithmetic - see Breakdown.kt), so those rows carry 'note_android', which the Kotlin runner uses instead of 'note'; Android has no insufficient-row badge, so its runner compares badge text for checked rows only. Every Breakdown row has at least one over-limit (tone 'warning') case - the runners assert that too.

cases.name: standalone_without_hitched_falls_back_to_axle_estimate
cases._note: Regression case for a real bug, fixed 2026-08-21 in both Python (compute_breakdown) and Kotlin (Breakdown.kt): a stand-alone reading with no real hitched (steer+drive) reading used to be treated the same as a real hitched+standalone pair, silently producing the wrong trailer total (11,380, the unadjusted axle reading) instead of the correct 14,225 axle-based estimate. Its Trailer Total row is correct in both platforms as of the 2026-08-21 fix, but this case is still tagged as requiring predictive_truck_estimate because its Tow Vehicle Total row's expected values (the standalone-only predictive branch) also depend on that capability, which Python already has and Kotlin doesn't yet (Round 2) - Python's own oracle bakes both capabilities into this input combination together, so there's no way to isolate just the trailer fix here without changing the scenario.

cases.name: zero_rated_limit_is_insufficient_not_a_crash
cases._note: Regression case for a real bug, found 2026-08-24 via a combinatorial sweep and fixed in both Python (compute_breakdown) and Kotlin (Breakdown.kt): a rated limit field (here front_gawr_lb) of exactly 0 used to pass an `is None`-only insufficient check, then get divided into computing pct - Python crashed outright with ZeroDivisionError, Kotlin's own `limit > 0` guard on that division stopped it from crashing but would have silently reported a false WARNING ("over limit") from the bogus zero instead of INSUFFICIENT. Fixed by treating 0 the same as absent for this field, matching standalone_weight_lb's existing truthy-not-just-null convention.

cases.name: pin_weight_pct_of_one_does_not_crash
cases._note: Regression case for a real bug, found 2026-08-24 via a combinatorial sweep and fixed in both Python (compute_breakdown) and Kotlin (Breakdown.kt): the axle-reading-estimate branch divides by `1 - pin_weight_pct` - exactly 1.0 (100% of the trailer's weight claimed as tongue weight, physically nonsensical) crashed with ZeroDivisionError in Python; a Kotlin Double doesn't crash on this (silently yields Infinity instead), but it's the same real bug. Fixed by narrowly snapping only the exact 1.0 value to 0.99 - a value *above* 1.0 (e.g. a caller sending a whole-number percentage like 15 instead of the fraction 0.15) is deliberately left alone, since it already fails loud with an obviously-wrong negative result instead of crashing or silently looking plausible.

cases.name: rounding_half_way_values_round_up
cases._note: Rounding-edge case: every row has a value sitting exactly on a .5 boundary (all exactly representable in binary floating point, so no implementation can disagree because of float noise). The agreed answer is round-half-UP (ties toward positive infinity), matching Kotlin's roundToInt/roundToLong and JavaScript's Math.round. Python's built-in round() is half-to-even and would give 5000 / 6000 / 16000 / 26000 / 32000 for the .5 readings below and 12 / 62 for the pct ties - breakdown.py rounds half-up explicitly to match (ADR-0007). Rows: Front Axle pct is exactly 12.5 (1000/8000); Rear Axle actual is 5000.5; Tow Vehicle Total actual is 6000.5 and its limit is 16000.5; Trailer Axle pct is exactly 62.5 (5000/8000); Trailer Total is 10000 / 16000 = exactly 62.5 (pin_weight_pct 0.5 makes the axle-reading estimate exact); Combined Rig Weight actual is 26000.5 and its limit is 32000.5.

cases.name: rounding_half_way_predictive_truck_estimate

See rounding_half_way_values_round_up for the agreed rule.
